hints: Calculate the downward distance fallen by ball $A$ in $2.5\text{ s}$ from rest: $s_A = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
Ball $B$ has been moving for $2.5 - 1.0 = 1.5\text{ s}$ with initial speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the upward distance moved: $s_B = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
Sum the two displacements to show that the height of the tower is $50\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
When the two balls pass each other, ball $A$ has been falling from the top of the tower for $t_A = 2.5\text{ s}$. Ball $B$ was projected $1.0\text{ s}$ later, so it has been traveling upward for:
$$t_B = 2.5 - 1.0 = 1.5\text{ s}$$

Calculate the downward displacement of ball $A$ dropped from rest ($u = 0$) under gravity $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s_A = ut_A + \frac{1}{2}gt_A^2 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(10)(2.5^2) = 5 \times 6.25 = 31.25\text{ m}$$

Calculate the upward displacement of ball $B$ projected with $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_B = ut_B - \frac{1}{2}gt_B^2 = 20(1.5) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(1.5^2) = 30 - 5(2.25) = 30 - 11.25 = 18.75\text{ m}$$

Because ball $A$ was dropped from the top and ball $B$ was projected from the bottom, the sum of their displacements equals the total height of the tower:
$$\text{Tower height} = s_A + s_B = 31.25 + 18.75 = 50\text{ m}$$

hints: Find the time $t_A$ when ball $A$ hits the ground by solving $50 = \frac{1}{2}gt_A^2$, which gives $t_A = \sqrt{10}\text{ s}$.
Deduce the time ball $B$ has been in motion: $t_B = t_A - 1 = \sqrt{10} - 1 \approx 2.16\text{ s}$.
Find the maximum height reached by ball $B$ using $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$, and check that it reaches this peak at $t = 2\text{ s}$ ($s = 20\text{ m}$).
Calculate the downward distance fallen by $B$ in the remaining $t_B - 2 = 0.1623\text{ s}$ using $\frac{1}{2}gt^2$, and add to $20\text{ m}$ for the total distance.
walkthrough:
First, calculate how long ball $A$ takes to fall from the top of the $50\text{ m}$ tower to the ground from rest ($u = 0$):
$$s = \frac{1}{2}gt_A^2$$
$$50 = 5t_A^2 \implies t_A^2 = 10 \implies t_A = \sqrt{10} \approx 3.16228\text{ s}$$

Ball $B$ was projected $1.0\text{ s}$ after ball $A$ was dropped, so the duration of ball $B$'s motion at this instant is:
$$t_B = t_A - 1 = \sqrt{10} - 1 \approx 3.16228 - 1 = 2.16228\text{ s} \approx 2.16\text{ s}$$

Next, analyze ball $B$'s vertical flight. It reaches its maximum height when its velocity becomes zero:
$$v = u - gt \implies 0 = 20 - 10t \implies t_{\text{up}} = 2\text{ s}$$

The height gained on the way up to the peak is:
$$s_{\text{up}} = \frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{20^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{400}{20} = 20\text{ m}$$

Because $t_B \approx 2.1623\text{ s} > 2.0\text{ s}$, ball $B$ reached its highest point and then fell downwards for an additional time of:
$$\Delta t = 2.16228 - 2.0 = 0.16228\text{ s}$$

Calculate the distance fallen from rest from the peak during this time:
$$s_{\text{down}} = \frac{1}{2}g(\Delta t)^2 = \frac{1}{2}(10)(0.16228)^2 = 5 \times 0.026335 \approx 0.1317\text{ m}$$

Total distance travelled is the sum of the distance going up and the distance coming down:
$$\text{Total distance} = s_{\text{up}} + s_{\text{down}} = 20 + 0.1317 \approx 20.1\text{ m}$$
